summary: Custom traffic-class rate configuration and throttle headers inquiry
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightScale is seeing frequent 429s that correlate with bursts from a webhook retry fanout. They have a Dedicated pool and want guidance on creating a custom traffic-class (low-latency vs bulk-ingest) so webhook retries don't consume low-latency route credits. They also asked whether Redwood can expose more granular throttle headers to enable client-side per-traffic-class backoff.

Impact:
- Intermittent 429s for user-facing chat flows during their nightly webhook replays (5-10% of requests during spikes).
- Customer requests config changes because they cannot isolate webhook traffic from chat traffic today.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool in us-east (prod).
- ~3x g4dn nodes reserved, autoscaling enabled for bursts.
- Ingests arrive via our webhook forwarder service which fanouts to 20 worker processes.

Customer ask:
1) Recommended configuration to create an isolated traffic class or route weight for webhook retries on Dedicated (so they don't impact chat).
2) Whether throttle headers can be augmented (e.g., X-RateLimit-Class, X-Route-Credit-Remaining) to let client workers back off per class instead of global backoff.
3) Suggested burst-smoothing policy (refill rates / credit windows) for high-frequency short bursts from retries.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Configure a webhook forwarder that fanouts to N=20 short-lived workers.
2) Each worker retries failed calls every ~200ms for a ~10s window (exponential backoff disabled for test).
3) Send a replay batch of 10k webhook events over 30s.
4) Observe 429s in the chat route logs around the same time; tail shows quota exhaustion on tenant token bucket.

Observed behavior: 429 responses include standard rate-limit headers (X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0; X-RateLimit-Reset: 1647264000) but no per-route/class metadata. The customer attached a sample 429 snippet below.
observed_headers:
HTTP/2 429
content-type: application/json
X-RateLimit-Limit: 60000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1647264000
X-Request-Id: rq_7a9b2c
body: {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"tenant token bucket exhausted"}
comments: 2026-03-13 10:12 - Sophie Ramirez (Support): Opened with customer request for traffic-class isolation + augmented headers. Customer provided spike timing and sample logs.

2026-03-13 11:05 - Liam Park (Eng): Acknowledged. Confirmed Dedicated pools currently support per-route weights but not first-class traffic tags. Asked for sample ingress metadata and if customer can send small pcap/logs of fanout pattern.

2026-03-13 14:30 - BrightScale (Customer): Provided worker concurrency histogram and timestamps. Noted chat latency spikes co-occur with replays. Asks if a short-term workaround exists while engineering evaluates longer term config options.
2026-03-13 15:10 - Sophie Ramirez (Support): Suggested temporary client-side splay (randomized retry jitter) and reducing per-worker concurrent connections to 4. Provided link to best-practice doc.

2026-03-14 09:00 - Liam Park (Eng): Investigation notes added. Proposed two options: 1) Add a low-priority route for webhook traffic with strict route weight in Dedicated; 2) Implement per-route token buckets in the edge layer (requires deployment change). Asked SRE for quota simulation in staging.

2026-03-14 12:05 - SRE Team: Ran quota simulation. With route weight=0.1 for webhook class, chat 99th pct latency unaffected during a 30s 10k replay in staging. Shared simulation logs in linked confluence page.
2026-03-14 13:40 - BrightScale: Agreed to test route-weight approach in staging and requested recommended header fields to read remaining credits per route if we later expose them.

2026-03-14 14:00 - Liam Park: Assigned follow-up ticket to implement a short-lived console toggle to create a 'traffic class' route weight in Dedicated; added to support ops tasks. Will follow up on header design separately.
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses:
- Webhook fanout creates concentrated microbursts that exhaust tenant-level token refill before route isolation can rebalance.
- Edge proxy currently attributes refill at tenant granularity; Dedicated per-route weighting exists but not as a first-class traffic tag customers can map from ingress metadata (e.g., X-Traffic-Class).
Findings:
- Simulation shows route-weighting (0.1) reduces cross-impact.
- No existing header exposes per-route remaining credits; rate-limit headers are tenant/global.
- Staging autoscaler handled the burst but token accounting still produced temporary exhaustion for chat route until route weights were applied.
Next steps:
- Provide step-by-step instructions for customer to create a low-priority route in Dedicated with weight=0.1 (short term).
- Internal backlog: design API for traffic-class tags and extended throttle headers (X-RateLimit-Class, X-Route-Credit-Remaining).
- Consider console toggle to create traffic classes for Dedicated customers as an MVP.
resolution:
Workaround provided: recommended immediate changes for BrightScale:
- Configure a dedicated low-priority route on their Dedicated pool for webhook replays and set route weight to 0.1. This isolates webhook credit usage from chat.
- Introduce client-side smoothing: add randomized jitter on retry, cap per-worker concurrency to 3-5 connections during replay windows.
- Schedule a staging run and share results in this ticket.

Planned follow-up actions (engineering):
- Create an internal feature ticket to evaluate exposing traffic-class mapping from ingress headers and adding extended rate-limit headers for per-class remaining credits.
- Add runbook entry in Confluence with route-weight example and recommended refill/window settings for webhook-like workloads.

Status: Customer to test route-weight in staging; eng to create feature ticket for header/traffic-class roadmap.
